title: Decode XORed Array
statement:
A secret array `arr` of `n` non-negative integers was turned into `encoded`, an array of length `n - 1` where `encoded[i]` is the bitwise XOR of `arr[i]` and `arr[i + 1]`. You receive `encoded` together with `first`, the value of `arr[0]`.

Rebuild and return `arr`. The input always determines exactly one such array.
notes:
## Intuition

XOR undoes itself: `x ^ y ^ y === x`. Since `encoded[i] = arr[i] ^ arr[i + 1]`, XOR-ing both sides with `arr[i]` gives `arr[i + 1] = arr[i] ^ encoded[i]`. Knowing `arr[0]` from `first`, each element reveals the next one. (A slower way recomputes every element as `first` XOR-ed with all earlier encoded values, which is O(n²).)

## Approach

1. Start `arr` with `first`.
2. For each `i` from 0 to `encoded.length - 1`, compute `next = arr[i] ^ encoded[i]`.
3. Append `next`; it becomes `arr[i + 1]` and feeds the following step.
4. Return `arr`, which now has `encoded.length + 1` elements.

## Example 1, step by step

`encoded = [1, 2, 3]`, `first = 1`, so `arr = [1]`.

- `i = 0`: `next = 1 ^ 1 = 0`, `arr = [1, 0]`.
- `i = 1`: `next = 0 ^ 2 = 2`, `arr = [1, 0, 2]`.
- `i = 2`: `next = 2 ^ 3 = 1`, `arr = [1, 0, 2, 1]`.

The answer is `[1, 0, 2, 1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one XOR per encoded value.
- Space: O(n) for the returned array (O(1) extra).

## Pitfalls

- The result has one more element than `encoded`; do not forget to start with `first`.
- Use the previously decoded value `arr[i]`, not `encoded[i - 1]`, as the partner of `encoded[i]`.
- `^` is XOR in JavaScript, Java and C, not a power operator.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `arr` | the decoded array, built left to right |
| `i` | index into `encoded`, also the index of the last decoded element |
| `next` | the value of `arr[i + 1]` |

narration.1: The input holds the n - 1 encoded pairs and arr[0].
narration.2: The first element is given, so the decoded array starts with it.
narration.3: Each encoded value links arr[i] to arr[i + 1]; visit them in order.
narration.4: XOR cancels arr[i] out of encoded[i], leaving arr[i + 1].
narration.5: Append it so it can unlock the next element.
narration.6: After the loop every encoded value has been used once.
narration.7: All n elements are decoded; return them.
